sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 09.02.2024 at about 9.00 a.m, the petitioner was riding a scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-09-JP-7761, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations when he reched near Metropole Circle, Devaraja Mohalla, Mysore City, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 which was coming from hind side of the Gangadhara Bora vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159576537/
1 petitioner's vehicle driven the same at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle from behind.

Due to the terrific impact the petitioner fell down on the road,
after which the left front wheel of the bus ran over on his right hand.
It is contended that immediately after the accident he was shifted to K.R. Hospital, Mysore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgeries.
During the course of treatment partial amputation of right upper limb done and was discharged with and regular follow up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards his treatment.
It is alleged that he was working in Deepak Tools Heat Treaters Limited and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident.
He fully disabled to avocation and loss earning capacity.
Looking to the nature of injuries he permanently disabled and was also undergone mental shock and agony.
The respondent being the RC owner and internal insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 is liable to pay compensation.

3. After service of notice, respondent KSRTC corporation filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent corporation emphatically denied the rashness & negligence pleaded on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus.

On the contrary it is submitted that on 09.02.2024 the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 was proceeding from Gundlupet via Sabara Bus station towards Veerajpet and same was driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules.

When the said KSRTC bus reached near Metropole Circle took turn towards left side of the road slolwy with showing signal, during that time one scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-09-JP-7761 ridden by its rider without following the traffic rules with high speed without wearing helmet and dashed agianst the left side body of the said KSRTC bus while took turn towards left side of the road and fell down on the road along with said scooter and sustained injuries.
Hence the accident occured purely on the part of the rider of the said scooter.
Further the petitioner colluded with the police had filed a false case against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Further the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. petitions and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.02.2024 at about 9.00 a.m., Near Metropole Circle, Devaraja Mohalla, Mysore City due to actionable negligence of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What Order or award ?

Ex's .P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.
Dr. S.A.
Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2.
Ex. P.14
& 15 were marked through him.
The MRO of K.R.Hospital was examined as PW.3.
Ex's .P16 to 20 were marked through this witness.

In order to prove its defence, the respondent Corporation got examined the driver who was driving the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 at the time of accident as RW.1.
6.
Arguments were addressed on both sides.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1 : From the evidence on record it is seen that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri.Subramaniyan.

C.N, Devaraja Traffic police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

8. No doubt during the course of his cross-examination, RW.1 (driver who was driving KSRTC Bus at the time of accident) denied the suggestion that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that took place due to his negligence.
He further admitted that at the time of accident he was driving the bus.
He admitted that FIR was lodged against him and the criminal case is pending and he was on bail.
But he has not challenged the charge sheet that is filed by the jurisdictional police against him.
Thus the unchallenged charge sheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of RW.1.

His self-serving statement cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident in order to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Therefore based on oral and documentary evidence, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 is proved.
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

ISSUE NO.2 :
9. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P12,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 03.09.1991.
This indicates that he was aged (32 years 5 months 6 days) 32 years on the date of accident.
10. No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :

sentences.text: The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 09.02.2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
11. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Mangled right upper extremily injury (Crush Injury).
Proximal humerus shaft fracture, Transeated crushed brachial axtery and nerves.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

As per the 3-discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.8 to 10, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the below mentioend hospitals:
 Hospital names From - to Total days  20.02.2024  Trauma Care Centre, 14.03.2024  Mysore  22.03.2024

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : (1) S/p amputation of right upper limb at the level of proximal lumerus under GA on 09.02.2024 (2) Debridement with STSG under GA on 18.03.2024.
12.
It is the definite assertion of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled.

Therefore he examined an Orthopedic Surgeon by name Dr. S.A.
Somashekara as PW.2 who deposed that on clinical examination, he found that the petitioner has 90% disability of right upper limb and 80% total whole body physical disability.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 admitted that he was not treated the petitioner and he has not seen the case sheet.
He admitted that limb is amputated at the level of shoulder, it was held by piece soft tissue.
During the course of his cross-examination he denied the suggestions with regard to the assessment of disability.

However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen Gangadhara Bora vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159576537/
4 that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

sentences.text: Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it could be culled out that petitioner being the 32 years age old has lost his right hand and because of this he may suffer huge pain and embarrassment in the society.
At his young age has to suffer this unbearable pain.
The petitioner has to depend on some one for his livelihood.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Whereas the petitioner can develop the new skills and opt for career transition.
The record reveals that the petitioner was working at Deepak Tools Heat Treaters Limited.
For a worker in a private company loosing his right hand is a great set back.
For the rest of his life he has to work without his right hand.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 60%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 60%.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of KSRTC bus.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
13. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

The case of an injured and disabled person, is however, more pitiable and the feeling of hurt, helplessness,
despair & often destitution ensures everyday.

The support that is needed by a severely handicapped person comes at an enormous price : physical, financial and emotional, not only on the victim but even moreso on his family & attendants and the stress saps their energy and destroys their equanimity.
The discharge summaries reveals that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 40 days.

Undoubtedly, during the said period he would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges, as some family member/s of the petitioner leaving his/her duties would have accompanied the petitioner to the hospital in order to take his care.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transport and nutrition.
Hence I feel it just and proper to award a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
14. PAIN & SUFFERINGS: Ex.P5 - wound certificate & Ex.P8 to 10-Discharge summaries show that due to accident PW.1 sustained : Right sided upper limb amputee at the level of proximal humerus.
15. As per medical records above said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex. P8 to 10 Discharge summaries goes to show that PW.1 was initially admitted to KR Hospital thereafter at Princes Krishnajammanni Trauma Care Centre, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for the period of 40 days where his right upper limb at the level of proximal humerus was removed by surgery.
It is not possible for the Tribunals to make a precise assessment of the pain and trauma suffered by a person whose limb is amputated as a result of accident.
Even if the victim of the accident gets artificial limb, he will suffer from different kinds of handicaps and social stigma throughout his life.

Therefore this Tribunal feels that the ends of the justice will be met by awarding the petitioner a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- in lieu of Pain, suffering & Trauma caused due to the amputation of his right hand Gangadhara Bora vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159576537/
5
above elbow.

16. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 4 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.66,000/- (16,500 X 4) under this head.
17.
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has produced 59- Medical bills as per Ex.P.11 amounting to Rs.63,370/- in total.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the cross examination of PW.1, so as to doubt the genuineness of the medical bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.63,370/- which is rounded off to Rs.63,400/- towards medical expenses.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.19,00,800/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 16 X 60/100) is awarded under this head.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded under this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL & OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
In his evidence affidavit the doctor witness has deposed that the petitioner needs a sophisticated prosthesis which is very expensive and runs into may lakhs.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 admitted that he has not issued any estimation in for prosthesis.
But in this context what deserves notice is that with technological advancement the quality of artificial limbs has improved and these advanced artificial limbs do come at substantive price.
Further like any other machinery they also require maintenance throughout the lifetime of the petitioner.
Considering all these factors, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head, which shall not carry any interest.

21. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 80,000-00 food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 2,00,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 66,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 63,400-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 19,00,800-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 3,00,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : 3,00,000-00 Total 29,10,200-00 Gangadhara Bora vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159576537/
6 22. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The Respondent being the RC owner & internal insurer of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0329 is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount.

With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
23. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,10,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/ RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 8th day of April - 2025)
(Shreyansh Doddamani)
